records.text: Shreev is a Gizmorium technician in Gadgetzan who modified Razzeric's seaforium booster to deliver more of its explosive payload but left its safety lock on. He warns Razzeric to be careful when setting it off, while Razzeric complains that the safety limits the booster's power.
Gunstan is a prospector of the Explorers' League found in Tanaris.

Krinkle Goodsteel sells blacksmithing supplies in Gadgetzan and takes specialized work. He charges fifteen gold for a Skeleton Key mold, packs skeletal fragments into it, and teaches customers how to forge the key's stem; both Apothecary Dithers and Alchemist Arbington send word ahead about the job. He says he is busy with many patrons and asks visitors to speed things up.
A Glasshide basilisk, this creature attacks with Crystal Flash when fighting.
A Glasshide gazer, this creature attacks with Crystal Gaze when fighting.
A Glasshide petrifier, this creature attacks with Petrify when fighting.
A scorpid hunter, this creature uses an attack when fighting.
A scorpid tail lasher, this creature uses Lash when fighting.
A scorpid dunestalker, this creature uses Venom Sting when fighting.
A starving Blisterpaw, this hyena-like creature attacks when fighting.
A Blisterpaw hyena, this creature attacks when fighting.
A rabid Blisterpaw, this creature uses Rabies when fighting.
Rocs are birds. The goretalon rocs of the Bonefields nest there and feed on the corpses of old mammoths, and their twisted claws and eggs are sought.
Fire rocs attack with Flamespit.
Searing rocs cast a spell when they enter combat.
Surf gliders are creatures found in the coastal areas of Tanaris.
Hazzali wasps are creatures of the Hazzali area of Tanaris that fight with poison.
A Hazzali swarmer found among the local creatures of Tanaris, it casts Silithid Swarm while out of combat.
A Hazzali worker found among the local creatures of Tanaris.
A Hazzali tunneler found among the local creatures of Tanaris, it uses Pierce Armor in combat.
A Hazzali sandreaver found in Tanaris, it uses Arcing Smash in combat.
A Centipaar wasp found among the local creatures of Tanaris, it uses Poison in combat.
A Centipaar stinger found among the local creatures of Tanaris, it uses Venom Sting in combat.
A Centipaar swarmer found among the local creatures of Tanaris, it casts Silithid Swarm in combat.
A Centipaar worker found among the local creatures of Tanaris, it uses Thrash in combat.
A Centipaar tunneler whose combat behavior includes piercing armor.
A Centipaar sandreaver that fights with a thrashing attack.
A land rager is an elemental that can become enraged in combat.
A giant of Tanaris that may carry an OOX-17/TN Distress Beacon, a gnomish device used to find Oglethorpe's missing homing robot.
Deep Dweller is a giant in Tanaris.
A Dune Smasher is a giant found in Tanaris.
A Dunemaul ogre found among Tanaris’s desert ruins, it settles into Battle Stance before combat.
A Dunemaul enforcer, one of the nomadic ogres of the desert compound, who uses Demoralizing Shout in battle. Andi Lynn in Gadgetzan wants the compound destroyed.
A Dunemaul ogre mage in the Tanaris desert, it casts Fireball in combat.
A Dunemaul brute of the desert compound, it attacks with Uppercut and is named as a target in Andi Lynn’s call to destroy the compound.
A Dunemaul warlock found in the Tanaris desert, it casts Shadow Bolt in combat.
A Thistleshrub Dew Collector in the Tanaris desert, it uses Entangling Roots in combat.
A strange thistleshrub rootshaper of Thistleshrub Valley, one of the creatures Tran'rek wants cleared from the valley.
A strange, gnarled thistleshrub of Thistleshrub Valley, one of the creatures Tran'rek wants cleared from the valley.

Alchemist Pestlezugg is an alchemist in Gadgetzan who studies the silithid threat. When given insect parts, he urges you to report to Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser; his research suggests the silithid may be controlled by an outside force. He also investigates the Gorishi hive and offers to prepare a lure to draw out its queen.
A Wastewander rogue, one of the nomads' stronger ranks. In combat, this stealthy attacker strikes its victim from behind.
A Wastewander thief among the nomads opposing Gadgetzan's water company. In combat, this thief can disarm an opponent.
A Wastewander shadow mage, counted among the nomads' stronger ranks. It can summon a voidwalker even while out of combat.
A Wastewander bandit among the nomads opposing Gadgetzan's water company. In combat, this bandit can gouge an opponent.
A Wastewander assassin, one of the nomads' stronger ranks. It can finish a badly wounded opponent with a decisive attack.
A Sandfury Hideskinner, a humanoid who fights with backstab.
Tooga is a lost, thirsty turtle who worries that Torta is waiting and repeatedly asks how much farther he must travel. He is devoted to his wife and greets her with delight when they are reunited.
Torta is Tooga’s impatient, hungry wife. After waiting for him, she complains that he returned without dinner, sends him to fetch food, and warns him not to get lost again.

Vizzklick supplies tailoring goods in Gadgetzan and is associated with the Undermarket. When told of Kovic’s defeat, he celebrates, accusing Kovic of years of shady trading that undercut honest traders, and promises a reward for the news.

Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle oversees the Gadgetzan Water Company's power sources and water wells. He treats their shortage as a business problem: he trades power sources for Wastewander water pouches, urges action against the nomads holding the wells, and emphasizes that the company expects to profit. His brisk, irreverent pitch mixes practical urgency with Goblin salesmanship.

Luglunket is a seasoned spigot operator for the Gadgetzan Water Company. Cheerfully recruiting help, he calls the Wastewander water pouches Gadgetzan's stolen water and offers a company care package for each five reclaimed. He frames the work as helping Gadgetzan help itself and keeping the community away from disaster.

Marin Noggenfogger is a thirsty goblin tinkerer whose experiments turn into a bid to create and sell a drink. He tries dew from desert dew collectors, rejects the first mixture as terrible-tasting, and asks his friend Sprinkle, an excellent chef, to improve it with some kick. He later mixes in her violet powder, proudly touts his Noggenfogger Elixir, and even admits to spilling a little during preparation.

Sprinkle is a chef in Gadgetzan who works on Marin Noggenfogger's drink experiments. She calls Marin a good guy but eccentric, and says he needs her help yet again. Her interest in cooking has a personal history: her sister did the cooking when Sprinkle was young, and Sprinkle discovered that Violet Tragan could make even her sister's concoctions taste good. She offers the mushroom as her secret ingredient and sends Marin violet powder, telling him he owes her a favor.

Fizzledowser surveys desert water for the Gadgetzan Water Company as nomads seize wells. After assistant Scrimshank disappears amid spreading Silithid, he fears the bugs may be controlled by a third party and sends his findings to scholar Zilzibin Drumlore for help. Protective of company information, he trusts longtime colleague Pestlezugg's judgment about sharing it.

Fizzgrimble welcomes the rare adventurer with an invitation to settle in for a chair and drink, then asks about entering the cage matches. As the local innkeeper, Fizzgrimble offers lodging and goods.

Curgle Cranklehop is an inventor helping Feralas’s druids preserve dwindling hippogryphs, which he says are harmed by the Gordunni ogres. He collects and assesses hippogryph eggs, distinguishing ordinary eggs from finer specimens and nurturing them in hope they hatch. His Super Egg-O-Matic supports that work.
Winkey is a humanoid in Tanaris who talks with visitors.

Marvon Rivetseeker is a scientist and treasure hunter whose home and workshop are in Ratchet. After his zeppelin crashes in Tanaris, he studies Gahz'ridian ornaments made by trolls and modeled on the hydra Gahz'rilla. He once explored the Sunken Temple, but recalls its serpent-statue chamber only vaguely; he suspects its stone circle hides greater treasure and warns of the evil within.

OOX-17/TN is a gnomish homing robot, recovered in Tanaris after going missing and badly damaged. Oglethorpe Obnoticus speaks through it and directs its recovery and escort toward a safe place for repairs. Its own systems announce emergency power, evasive action, combat analysis, and danger, punctuating these alerts with a mechanical “CLUCK.” It can stand and travel under its own power, and its flight systems can engage rockets for transport to Booty Bay.
Gimblethorn is a banker in Booty Bay who offers access to banking services.

Trenton Lighthammer is the Mithril Order's blacksmith, known around Tanaris as the Mithril Kid. A pupil of Galvan the Ancient, he still seeks to master ornate mithril patterns. He remembers the Zul'Farrak troll warband that taught him to fear Sul'thraze; a jagged scar marks his face. He prizes troll temper for his craft and celebrates the Order's members.
Bera Stonehammer is a gryphon master who offers flight routes. When attacked, Bera calls for guards, and the response summons an enraged gryphon.
Bulkrek Ragefist is a wind rider master who offers flight routes. When attacked, Bulkrek calls for guards, and the response summons an enraged wyvern.

Caliph Scorpidsting is identified on a Gadgetzan Water Company bounty notice as leader of the Wastewander outlaws. The notice accuses him of murdering company employees and stealing or seizing its resources and property; it offers a reward for proof of his death.

A Southsea pirate at Lost Rigger Cove. The pirates have stopped honoring the Steamwheedle Cartel's protection payments, and Security Chief Bilgewhizzle wants them taught a lesson. This pirate fights with Strike.

A Southsea freebooter at Lost Rigger Cove, part of the group targeted by Security Chief Bilgewhizzle after the pirates stopped honoring the Steamwheedle Cartel’s protection payments. This freebooter shoots at range and may flee for help when badly wounded.

A Southsea dock worker at Lost Rigger Cove, among the pirates targeted by Security Chief Bilgewhizzle over their refusal to honor the Steamwheedle Cartel’s protection payments. In combat, this worker uses Head Crack.

A Southsea swashbuckler at Lost Rigger Cove, part of the group targeted by Security Chief Bilgewhizzle after the pirates stopped honoring the Steamwheedle Cartel’s protection payments. This fighter uses Disarm and may flee for help when badly wounded.

Tran'rek is a scheming, deal-minded resident of Gadgetzan. He trades scarab-colony information for uncracked shells, including a shipment for his cousin Krazek in Booty Bay. He wants a way back into Thistleshrub Valley, wary of its thistleshrubs, and has a plan to make money from unusually sticky tar.

Stoley tends the bar at Steamwheedle Port and is caught up in a rum wager with his old friend, “Sea Wolf” MacKinley. After Captain Cuergo steals his last shipment, Stoley asks for help recovering it so he can supply the bottle and settle their argument over whether Steamwheedle rum beats Booty Bay's. He insists he is not afraid to pay up; he simply has no rum to give MacKinley yet.

Security Chief Bilgewhizzle serves as Steamwheedle Port's security chief and must stay there to keep the peace. Because the Cartel cannot spare him to confront pirates who stopped paying protection money, he deputizes help against the Southsea gang at Lost Rigger Cove. He also handles pirate arrests under Steamwheedle's legal terms, including Andre Firebeard's case.

Andre Firebeard is a pirate wanted for crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan. The posted warrant authorizes lethal force in his apprehension and allows his head to stand in for him at a hearing if he is dead or otherwise indisposed.
Qizzik is a banker in Tanaris who gives visitors access to the bank.

Dirge Quikcleave is an ambitious butcher and cook who calls his clamlette his latest culinary masterpiece and offers to teach exotic cuisine. He pursues prized chimaerok meat for his signature Kickin’ Chimaerok Chops, and cheerfully defends even leather as a high-protein snack when caught spitting it out.

Nixx Sprocketspring teaches Goblin Engineering in Gadgetzan with swagger and a taste for explosives. He asks aspiring goblin engineers to show him their work so he can look for goblin techniques, and boasts that goblin engineering means know-how. His praise of a steady hand comes with a pointed jab at gnomes.
Pikkle is a mining trainer who teaches mining to those who ask.
Wrinkle Goodsteel is a superior armorer in the area. He offers goods for browsing, serving as a local source for armor and other wares.
Blizrik Buckshot is a gunsmith in the area. His shop offers goods for browsing, marking him as a local source for firearms and related wares.
Gikkix is a fisherman who sells food to travelers nearby.
Jabbey keeps a general goods shop and sells everyday supplies to travelers.
Occulus is a dragonkin found in Tanaris.
Chronalis is a dragon who fights with magic, casting more spells as his health falls.
Tick is a dragon who fights with magic, casting another spell as his health falls.
Warleader Krazzilak is a humanoid warleader.
Jin'Zallah the Sandbringer is a humanoid.
Omgorn the Lost is a humanoid fighter who uses Mortal Strike and becomes enraged as his health falls.
Cyclok the Mad is a humanoid spellcaster who uses Arcane Bolt and Arcane Explosion in combat.
Kregg Keelhaul is a humanoid who fights with Cleave and Strike.
Soriid the Devourer is a beast. In combat, it can use Pierce Armor and Rend.
Haarka the Ravenous is a beast.
The Greater Firebird is a beast.
Murderous Blisterpaw is a beast.

Yeh'kinya studies troll prophecy for a way to contain Hakkar's essence. He says he fears the god's return could bring catastrophe and that the essence might be abused. After an avatar is defeated, he offers a spell to summon another, saying that further defeats could weaken Hakkar.
Zalashji is a humanoid in Tanaris who has tasks for travelers.
Auctioneer Beardo provides auction services.
An elemental of Tanaris that carries an OOX-17/TN Distress Beacon, a gnomish device used to find Oglethorpe's missing homing robot.
Buzzek Bracketswing is an engineering trainer who is developing a plan to transport oil underground between major cities. He says others dismiss the idea as a pipe dream.
A tiger kept as a riding mount.
A skeletal undead mount.

Gaeriyan is an elusive figure in a rocky crevice in the mountains north of the graveyard outside Gadgetzan, who speaks only to those who drink a Videre Elixir and take on another form. He points toward a distinctive gravestone and its secrets in the Linken mystery. He remarks on how rarely anyone seeks him out; he can cast Shroud of Death.
Ground Pounder is a giant that casts an ability when hurt.
Living Storm is an elemental.
A Gadgetzan guard assigned to protect the town’s interests in Un’Goro, this bruiser answers danger with sharp threats and a net.
Yorba Screwspigot sees a chance to profit from his brother Ribbly’s newfound worth and asks for help through his sister Yuka, who has been searching for Ribbly and tracked him to the Burning Steppes.
Laziphus is Gadgetzan’s stable master, helping visitors stable pets and recover lost companions.

Prospector Ironboot studies the Mosh’aru Tablets and fears their writings reveal a threat tied to Hakkar’s return. He sends others to find the remaining tablets, then urges them to confront Yeh’kinya and demand the egg before Hakkar can be reborn.

Quinn Yorick is a Deathstalker sent with his brother Rane Yorick to scout northern Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. The ghoul Ivar the Foul mauled him; he is recovering with a potion while Rane worries Ivar may return before Quinn heals.

Andi Lynn is concerned about the Dunemaul ogres who have established a compound south of Gadgetzan and whose bands have spread across Tanaris, including the old troll ruins. She sees their growing force as a threat and urges its destruction, identifying Gor'marok the Ravager as their leader. Her request focuses on breaking the band by defeating its forces and ending Gor'marok's leadership.

Narain Soothfancy is a retired engineer and master soothsayer, a gnome who boasts of psychic powers but can mistake a visitor’s purpose. He is trying to translate Azuregos’s ledger from Draconic and needs his stolen scrying goggles, taken by Stewvul, his former best friend. His elaborate plans also call for a 500-pound chicken and a copy of Draconic for Dummies.
Gor'marok the Ravager is the leader of the nomadic ogres occupying the Dunemaul Compound in Tanaris. He is a melee fighter who cleaves and strikes mortally, and grows enraged when badly hurt.
Steeljaw Snapper is a beast found in several parts of Tanaris.

A Thorium Brotherhood recipe supplier who trades Imperial Plate plans for thorium bars and teaches the craft for the same payment. His dealings are brisk and hard-nosed: he calls the exchange a hot deal, jokes that the cost will bankrupt you, and has little patience for complaints.

A gnomish engineer who says he built the Matter Transporter from technology recovered by gnomes exploring Gnomeregan. He needs a skilled Gnomish Engineer to make a beacon attuned to it and welcomes ideas for improving the device.

A fashion designer who claims to choose what Azeroth's kings, queens and Warchiefs wear, charging the elite handsomely. She has Southsea pirate hats gathered at Lost Rigger Cove to clean, personalize and resell, and treats the hired help sent by the Cartel with lofty impatience.

Anachronos seeks to protect the Scepter of the Shifting Sands from misuse. In his account, Staghelm’s betrayal led him to gather its fragments and entrust a divided scepter to the four Aspects. He regrets assuming this would prevent its restoration by those seeking chaos. He expects a champion to challenge C’Thun and urges a first strike to avoid repeating past mistakes.
O'Reily is a beast found in Tanaris.

Meridith remembers rescuing a gnome from the wreckage of a crashed flying machine and speaks of loving Narain Soothfancy. She finds the ocean floor peaceful and offers a song associated with easier travel through rough seas.

Elder Ragetotem is honored with a token in return for homage. He recalls a time when his people hunted for glory and honor, and wonders whether life has changed. Other elders recognize him by name among their peers.

Elder Dreamseer is honored with a token in return for homage. Like Elder Ragetotem, Dreamseer recalls a time when the people hunted for glory and honor, and wonders whether life has changed. Dreamseer recognizes Ragetotem and other elders by name.
Southsea Kidnapper is a Southsea humanoid of Lost Rigger Cove. It may carry a Southsea Pirate Hat, the kind Haughty Modiste wants for her fashion trade.

Mux Manascrambler works on spectral devices in Gadgetzan, including an extra-dimensional ghost revealer and an ectoplasmic distiller. Proud of the engineering but short of funds and manpower, Mux recruits help to gather materials and ectoplasm, explaining that different climates give the dead's spectral fabric different consistencies. Mux regrets not buying a suitable rod from an imp in Winterspring and urges the buyer to hold the merchant to the quoted price.

Rumsen Fizzlebrack speaks for goblins seeking to repair relations after past trespasses. In “War at Sea,” he asks for mageweave and strong flux for sails and guns against the Bloodsail Buccaneers, while warning that goblins remember their grievances.

Alexston Chrome welcomes guests to the Tavern of Time, invites them to rest, and offers a drink he describes as exceptionally aged. His promise that the tavern has “all the time in the world” gives his hospitality a time-themed flourish.
Max Luna is an arena battlemaster who handles joining the Battle Ground.
Katrina Turner is a humanoid in Tanaris.
Bip Nigstrom is an Arena Organizer who answers questions about forming a guild.

Andormu is a Keeper of Time who is monitoring disturbances in the timeways. He is concerned that the beings altering them are appearing more often and may threaten the timeline. With the master away, he sees himself and his fellow Keepers as responsible for protecting the stream, and is wary of putting them at risk. His exchange with Nozari shows familiarity and occasional dry humor.

Nozari is a Keeper of Time and Andormu’s sister, whom she calls her equal. She listens as he explains that beings are tampering with the timeways, then agrees to act with him. Their exchange is familiar but pointed: she objects when he speaks down to her and reminds him that she once helped him in a temporal vortex.
Zaladormu is dragonkin in Tanaris.

Soridormi is a bronze dragon of the Scale of the Sands who identifies as the Aspect's prime mate and describes an unusually close connection to time. Sensing a small ripple around the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Soridormi seeks to stop an unknown attempt to alter an event whose outcome shapes later history. Soridormi rewards allies with rings infused by remnants of the Well of Eternity and gladly strengthens those gifts as their service and standing grow.
Arazmodu is dragonkin affiliated with the Scale of the Sands.
A dragonkin custodian of time.
A dragonkin called Warden of Time.
An imprisoned Infinite Dragonspawn is a dragonkin.
A sable jaguar specimen, a beast.
A Darkwater Crocolisk Specimen.
A Blackfang Tarantula Specimen.
A humanoid Lodaeron Sentry Specimen. Its name suggests a sentry role.

Galgrom is a provisioner stranded with his brother between their own time and the present. They fear leaving could cause a temporal paradox and wait for the dragons to return them to their proper timeline. He cannot say how long they have been stuck, and offers cheese.

Bortega supplies reagents and poisons. Bortega says she has the voice of a young orc woman, remarks that time travel does strange things to a body, and adds that “it’s 250 years,” without clarifying what that span measures.
Yarley says he has been stuck here for as long as he can remember. He recalls being an armorer in his former life and offers to repair equipment.

Andormu is a Keeper of Time who directs visitors through the Caverns’ timeways, including following the Custodian of Time. He frames interference with Thrall’s escape from Durnholde and Medivh’s opening of the Dark Portal as threats to the world’s continued existence, and directs travelers to agents in Old Hillsbrad and the Black Morass.
Nozari is one of the Keepers of Time.

The Steward of Time is a Keeper who guides visitors toward the master’s lair. He warns mortals that dangers beyond the hall are unknown in their world and offers a flight down, carried out by one of his brothers.
Vixton Pinchwhistle is the official Arena Vendor for the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit. He greets visitors casually and sells the circuit's goods to those with enough reputation.
A humanoid sniper associated with Gadgetzan, in Tanaris.
Alurmi is the Keepers of Time quartermaster in the Caverns of Time, where she sells goods to visitors.
The Tanaris Flame Warden tends the Alliance festival flame. She welcomes visitors who come to honor it and urges the Alliance to honor its fires and desecrate Horde fires.
The Tanaris Flame Keeper tends the Horde festival flame. He welcomes visitors who come to honor it and urges the Horde to honor its fires and desecrate Alliance fires.

Don Carlos is an old man in Tanaris who says he once wore his unusual hat as a challenge and was never beaten. He now drinks and fishes rather than dueling, and waits for an old friend. His story recalls that he was beaten once in Old Hillsbrad; he trades the returned hat for the challenger’s.
A humanoid Stratholme citizen specimen.
A humanoid Stratholme resident specimen.
A Lordaeron footman specimen in Tanaris.
A Stratholme child specimen in Tanaris.
A cat specimen in Tanaris.
Argex Irongut is a merchant whose goods visitors can browse.
Argex Irongut is a veteran arena vendor.
Ecton Brasstumbler is an Apprentice Arena Vendor who sells goods to visitors.
Evee Copperspring is an Arena Vendor who sells goods to visitors.
Argex Irongut is a Veteran Arena Vendor who sells goods to visitors.
Evee Copperspring is an Arena Vendor who sells goods to visitors.
Ecton Brasstumbler is an apprentice arena vendor.
Ecton Brasstumbler is an Apprentice Arena Vendor who sells goods to visitors.
Evee Copperspring is an Arena Vendor who sells goods to visitors.
Argex Irongut is a Veteran Arena Vendor who sells goods to visitors.
Blazzek the Biter sells exceptional arena weaponry.
Blazzek the Biter is a vendor of exceptional arena weaponry.
Blazzek the Biter is a vendor of exceptional arena weaponry.

place_records.text: You are in Tanaris, a desert in Kalimdor held by neither the Alliance nor the Horde. Its main settlements are Gadgetzan, where engineers and tradesmen run the water company, and Steamwheedle Port, where a security chief keeps the peace against pirates who stopped paying protection money. Blisterpaw hyenas and scorpids roam the sands, Wastewander nomads hold the wells, and silithid insects are spreading across the desert and draining the water pools.

You are in Gadgetzan, a desert town in Tanaris with its own water company. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle runs the wells and power sources and urges action against the nomads holding the wells. Alchemist Pestlezugg studies the silithid spreading through the sands, and Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser fears for his missing assistant Scrimshank. It has an inn and a flight master.

You are in Steamwheedle Port, a town in Tanaris. Security Chief Bilgewhizzle must stay to keep the peace, so he deputizes help against the Southsea pirates who stopped paying protection money. The fashion designer Haughty Modiste commissions Southsea pirate hats for resale, and Stoley tends the bar. Scorpid hunters roam here too.

You are in Sandsorrow Watch, an area of Tanaris. Sandfury firecallers, axe throwers and hideskinners, along with glasshide basilisks, starving blisterpaw hyenas and scorpid tail lashers, are the dangers here.
You are in Thistleshrub Valley, an area of Tanaris. Thistleshrub dew collectors and rootshapers are its main dangers, along with gnarled thistleshrubs.

You are in the Gaping Chasm, a stretch of desert southeast of Gadgetzan. Junior Surveyor Scrimshank went missing here, and a dragonkin custodian of time is found in the chasm. Hazzali wasps, swarmers, stingers and sandreavers infest it.
You are in the Noxious Lair, where Centipaar insects are draining the water pools that used to be here. Centipaar stingers, wasps, swarmers, workers and tunnelers are its dangers.
You are in Dunemaul Compound, an area of Tanaris. Dunemaul brutes, enforcers and warlocks are its dangers, with rabid blisterpaw hyenas and scorpid dunestalkers roaming nearby.
You are in Eastmoon Ruins, an area of Tanaris. Dunemaul warlocks, enforcers and ogre mages prowl the ruins, along with glasshide gazers, scorpid dunestalkers and blisterpaw hyenas.
You are in Waterspring Field, an area of Tanaris. Wastewander shadow mages, rogues, thieves and assassins are its main dangers, along with scorpid tail lashers and glasshide gazers.

You are in Land's End Beach, a shore in Tanaris. Meridith the Mermaiden remembers rescuing a gnome from a crashed flying machine, and she speaks of loving Narain Soothfancy. Surf gliders are the danger here.
You are in Wavestrider Beach, a shore in Tanaris with its own spirit healer. Wastewander rogues, shadow mages, thieves, bandits and assassins are the dangers here, along with scorpid hunters.
You are in Uldum, a compound in the Tanaris desert whose entry is guarded by a Stone Watcher of Norgannon, who admits no one without the platinum discs. Dune smashers prowl the sands outside.

You are in Valley of the Watchers, a part of Tanaris where Prospector Gunstan of the Explorers' League, an Alliance man, is found. Glasshide petrifiers, rabid blisterpaws, dune smashers and scorpid dunestalkers roam the valley.
You are in Southmoon Ruins, a crumbled site in the Tanaris desert now home to rabid blisterpaws, glasshide gazers, searing rocs, dunemaul ogres, dunemaul enforcers and scorpid dunestalkers.
You are in Lost Rigger Cove, a cove in Tanaris overrun by Southsea swashbucklers, freebooters, pirates and dock workers. Andre Firebeard and Kregg Keelhaul are among the most notable of them.
You are in Noonshade Ruins, a ruined site in Tanaris where wastewander thieves and bandits prowl among scorpid hunters, starving blisterpaws and glasshide basilisks.

You are in Broken Pillar, a stretch of Tanaris where Marvon Rivetseeker, a scientist and treasure hunter, studies Gahz'ridian ornaments that trolls made long ago, modeled after the hydra Gahz'rilla. Scorpid tail lashers, blisterpaw hyenas, glasshide gazers and fire rocs roam here.

You are in Abyssal Sands, a sandy stretch of Tanaris where a spirit healer offers a return to the living for a price, while cautioning that it may not yet be your time. Blisterpaw hyenas, fire rocs, glasshide gazers, scorpid tail lashers, scorpid dunestalkers and glasshide basilisks roam the sands.

You are in Southbreak Shore, a stretch of Tanaris where Galgrom, a provisioner stranded here with his brother, waits for dragons to return them to their own time, fearing that leaving could cause a temporal paradox. Surf gliders, coast striders, blisterpaw hyenas and deep dwellers roam the shore.

You are in Caverns of Time, a hall of the Keepers of Time where the Steward of Time guides visitors toward the master's lair and warns that dangers past the hall are unknown to mortals. Anachronos, who seeks to keep the Scepter of the Shifting Sands from misuse, is found here as well. Chronalis and Occulus haunt the halls.
You are in South Seas, a part of Tanaris where a ransom note demands money from a gnome for the return of a book its writers are holding.
